record.paper_title: A Nonequilibrium Statistical Ensemble Formalism. Maxent-Nesom: Concepts, Construction, Application, Open Questions and Criticisms
record.original_question: For a dissipative nonequilibrium many-body system, what statistical operator should replace the instantaneous generalized canonical distribution, given that the instantaneous MaxEnt operator does not satisfy the Liouville equation, does not describe dissipative processes, does not supply a correct kinetic theory, and does not give correct averages for observables outside the selected basic variables?

evidence.quote: The statistical operator of Eq. (19) has the form of an instantaneous generalized canonical distribution, and an immediate question is if it properly provides a nonequilibrium statistical mechanics for dissipative systems. The answer is on the negative.
The question is then to find the proper nonequilibrium statistical operator that MaxEnt-NESOM should provide.

The way out of the difficulties pointed out above is contained in the idea set forward by John Kirkwood in the decade of the forties. He pointed out that the state of the system at time t is strongly dependent on all the previous evolution of the nonequilibrium processes that have been developing in it.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let a dissipative many-body quantum system be described on a Hilbert space with Hamiltonian H = H_0 + H', where H_0 is the "relevant" part (whose eigenstates define the basic dynamics) and H' is the interaction responsible for dissipation. Suppose one selects a set of basic dynamical variables {P_j} (Hermitian operators) whose nonequilibrium macroscopic averages Q_j(t) = Tr{P_j ρ(t)} are taken as the contracted description of the macrostate. The instantaneous generalized canonical (MaxEnt) statistical operator at time t is defined as the operator ρ̄(t) that maximizes the Gibbs–Shannon entropy S[ρ] = −Tr{ρ ln ρ} subject to the constraints Tr{P_j ρ̄(t)} = Q_j(t) and Tr{ρ̄(t)} = 1, namely
   ρ̄(t) = exp{−φ(t) − Σ_j F_j(t) P_j},
where φ(t) is fixed by normalization and {F_j(t)} are Lagrange multipliers conjugate to {Q_j(t)}.

It is known that ρ̄(t) (i) does not satisfy the Liouville equation, (ii) cannot describe irreversible dissipative evolution, (iii) does not yield a closed kinetic theory for the {Q_j(t)}, and (iv) does not generally give the correct averages of observables lying outside the span of {P_j}.

Problem. Construct, on the basis of ρ̄(t), a statistical operator ρ_ε(t) that (a) reduces to ρ̄(t) in an appropriate "initial-condition" sense, (b) satisfies the Liouville equation with infinitesimal sources breaking time-reversal symmetry, (c) incorporates memory of the past history of the nonequilibrium evolution of the system (in the spirit of Kirkwood's observation that the state at time t depends on all prior evolution of the irreversible processes), and (d) provides a proper basis for a nonequilibrium statistical mechanics yielding correct dissipative kinetic equations and averages of observables not included among the {P_j}.

Specifically, give an explicit closed-form expression for ρ_ε(t) in terms of ρ̄(t') for t' ≤ t together with a memory/weighting kernel involving a positive infinitesimal ε → 0+ taken after the thermodynamic limit, and verify that ρ_ε(t) satisfies a modified Liouville equation
   ∂ρ_ε/∂t + (i/ℏ)[H, ρ_ε] = −ε (ρ_ε − ρ̄),
so that ρ_ε is the desired proper nonequilibrium statistical operator replacing ρ̄(t).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem corresponds to the well-known construction by Zubarev (and independently formulated in the Kirkwood-inspired NESOM framework) of the nonequilibrium statistical operator. The answer is the memory-weighted operator ρ_ε(t) = exp{ln ρ̄(t) − ∫_{−∞}^{t} dt' e^{ε(t'−t)} d/dt'[ln ρ̄(t',t'−t)]_{H}} (with ε→0+ after the thermodynamic limit), which satisfies the Liouville equation with Gibbs-type infinitesimal sources. This construction is standard and well-documented in the literature on NESOM.

status_evidence.title: Zubarev nonequilibrium statistical operator
status_evidence.snippet: Zubarev's nonequilibrium statistical operator method generalizes the Gibbs ensemble by incorporating memory of past evolution via an infinitesimal source breaking time-reversal symmetry.
status_evidence.claim: The proper NESOM operator is the Zubarev-Kirkwood memory-weighted statistical operator.

status_evidence.title: Predictive Statistical Mechanics (Luzzi, Vasconcellos, Ramos)
status_evidence.snippet: The way out of the difficulties is contained in the idea set forward by John Kirkwood... the state of the system at time t is strongly dependent on all the previous evolution.
status_evidence.claim: Resolution uses Kirkwood's memory idea, yielding the NESOM statistical operator.
